facts.text: Genetic algorithms, NSGA-II, Bayesian optimization and gradient-free search are search procedures for finding good settings when settings can only be judged by running slow simulations.
facts.quote: These are the search procedures the booklet names for finding good settings when the only way to judge a setting is to run it through a slow simulation and see what happens.

facts.text: The optimization methods listed in the glossary entry are gradient-free, which suits closed-loop braking tests because outcomes jump from stopping in time to collision at a threshold.
facts.quote: All the methods below are gradient-free, which suits closed-loop braking tests, where the result jumps from "stopped in time" to "collision" at a threshold.

facts.text: Genetic algorithms, also called evolutionary methods, score a population of candidate settings by simulation, retain better candidates, and create new candidates by mixing and slightly altering the survivors.
facts.quote: Genetic algorithms, also called evolutionary methods, keep a population of candidate settings, score each by simulation, keep the better ones, and breed new candidates by mixing and slightly altering the survivors.

facts.text: NSGA-II (Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II), attributed to Deb and colleagues in 2002, handles several objectives at once by evolving the whole Pareto front.
facts.quote: NSGA-II (Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II, Deb and colleagues, 2002) is the version for several objectives at once; it evolves the whole Pareto front.

facts.text: The booklet rates genetic algorithms and NSGA-II as robust and easy to run in parallel, but hungry for evaluations.
facts.quote: The booklet rates these methods robust and easy to run in parallel, but hungry for evaluations [Chapter 9].

facts.text: Bayesian optimization fits a surrogate model to previous results and uses model uncertainty to select the most informative next setting, evaluates that setting, and repeats.
facts.quote: It fits a surrogate model to the results so far, uses the model's uncertainty to pick the most informative next setting, runs it, and repeats.

facts.text: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization variants seek the frontier, while safe variants restrict exploration to settings believed safe.
facts.quote: Multi-objective variants seek the frontier, and "safe" variants keep exploration inside settings believed safe.

facts.text: Bayesian optimization weaknesses include surrogate error, poor scaling beyond roughly 20 parameters, difficulty around discontinuities, adaptive bias, and the risk that an apparently safe extrapolation is wrong.
facts.quote: Its weaknesses are surrogate error, poor scaling beyond roughly 20 parameters, trouble around discontinuities, adaptive bias, and the danger that an apparently safe extrapolation is wrong [Chapter 9].

facts.text: The booklet matches response-surface methods to a handful of smooth parameters or a few continuous constants.
facts.quote: The booklet also names response-surface methods for a handful of smooth parameters

facts.text: ROC (receiver operating characteristic) operating-point selection is used for the detector threshold alone and must be followed by closed-loop evaluation because ROC selection ignores braking timing.
facts.quote: ROC (receiver operating characteristic) operating-point selection for the detector threshold alone, which must be followed by closed-loop evaluation because it ignores braking timing [Chapter 9].

facts.text: The booklet matches evolutionary methods to simulation tuning of the trade-off between misses, nuisance braking and margin.
facts.quote: evolutionary methods for the misses-against-nuisance-against-margin trade-off in simulation

facts.text: The booklet matches Bayesian optimization to expensive evaluations, such as hardware-in-the-loop rigs or physical runs.
facts.quote: Bayesian optimization is for expensive evaluations, such as hardware-in-the-loop or physical runs.

facts.text: The booklet reports no published off-road braking application for the tuning methods it matches to jobs: response surfaces, evolutionary methods and Bayesian optimization.
facts.quote: None has a published off-road braking application [Chapter 9].
